title: Orthodox: faith does not justify as a meritorious work—mode still disputed
source_text: VIII. Ad ista respiciant Doctores Orthodoxi, dum negant fidem nos justificare ut opus. Nec enim per hoc aliud significatum intendunt, quam quod fides non sit justificationis causa, ut loquuntur Scholae, formalis, vel meritoria, id est, ut jam diximus, justitiae illius, qua coram districto Dei judicio stare possimus, pars, vel meritum, seu pretium quo illa acquiratur, atque obtineatur. Sed, quamvis de his consentiant Theologi Reformati, non convenit tamen inter illos, qua ratione fides justificare dicatur.
pass_a_gloss: Let the Orthodox Doctors look to these things when they deny that faith justifies us as a work. For by this they intend no other meaning than that faith is not the formal or meritorious cause of justification, as the Schools speak—that is, as we have already said, a part of that righteousness by which we can stand before God's strict judgment, or the merit or price by which it is acquired and obtained. But although Reformed theologians agree on these things, they do not yet agree among themselves by what reason faith is said to justify.
pass_b_english: Denying that faith justifies 'as a work' means it is not formal/meritorious cause.
Reformed agree on that—but still dispute how faith justifies.

choices.why: Faith is not the meritorious price of justification.
